recentItems.title: Separated by war in Gaza: A family’s journey home | Witness Documentary
recentItems.description:
A day after a "ceasefire" is announced, Captain Moumen’s family sets off on Gaza’s long coastal road, carrying everything they own on their backs. They leave the Nuseirat refugee camp, where they have been taking refuge from constant bombing and head north, where Moumen awaits their arrival.

As Moumen’s wife and children trek through difficult terrain, he waits anxiously at the end of the road. With no signal to call and hundreds of thousands of people crossing, trying to locate them becomes an impossible mission.

Gaza Family Reunion is a documentary film by Mohammed Sawwaf, Salah al-Haw, Ibrahim al-Otla and Mohammed Masharawi.

recentItems.title: Brief: Settlers attack Palestinians and diplomats in occupied West Bank | The Take
recentItems.description:
This week: 373 days after the declaration of a ceasefire in Gaza, Israel has killed at least 1,511 Palestinians there.   Israeli settlers have carried out more than 300 attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since the beginning of October. Gaza continues to shrink. The UN's longest-running peacekeeping mission is set to end in December. Israel has killed at least 74,469 Palestinians in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

recentItems.title: Yemen cholera cases triple as conflict fuels deadly outbreak
recentItems.description:
The World Health Organization (WHO) says suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in three weeks. 
That's placing a burden on hospitals already battling to treat people injured in the latest conflict.
The disease is spread through contaminated food and water.

Saaid Said Omar, acting country director for Islamic Relief in Yemen, tells Al Jazeera cholera is spreading fast in overcrowded displacement camps with no clean water or latrines, putting children under five, pregnant women and the elderly most at risk.

recentItems.title: Why Netanyahu doesn't want Israelis abroad voting in the election
recentItems.description:
Unlike most countries, Israel does not allow absentee voting. With the general elections just weeks away, the governing Likud party has challenged efforts to help people travel to Israel to cast their ballots. 
Surveys suggest a significant number of voters abroad oppose the current government, and their votes could be a deciding factor in determining whether Benjamin Netanyahu can hold onto power. 

Al Jazeera's Julide Ayger explains.

recentItems.title: How the Palestinian Israeli vote could reshape Israel's election
recentItems.description:
Nearly 1.2 million Palestinian citizens of Israel have the right to vote in the Israeli elections.
These are the Palestinians who remained on their land when Israel was created in 1948.
Their vote could shape the next government, but it all depends on turnout.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim looks at the voting bloc that could be a game changer.

recentItems.title: El Nino threatens Zimbabwe harvest as drought puts millions at risk of hunger
recentItems.description:
The UN says the effects of the El Nino climate phenomenon could put more than six million people at risk of hunger in Zimbabwe.
The government is warning farmers not to rush into planting after the first rain.
But with just one growing season, waiting carries risks of its own.

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque reports.
